title: Runtime Semantic Discovery for Evolving Action Alphabets
abstract: arXiv:2610.28682v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Runtime Verification typically assumes a fixed alphabet of observable actions. This assumption becomes fragile in evolving software systems, where updates, reconfigurations, or architectural changes may rename, split, or fuse actions while preserving the system's high-level intent. In these cases, previously valid monitors and specifications may become misaligned with the running system.   In this paper, we study runtime semantic discovery, namely the problem of identifying whether newly observed actions play the same operational role as previously known ones, without reconstructing a global behavioral model. To this end, we propose a local and runtime-computable notion of action similarity based on the neighbor contexts in which actions occur within execution traces. translated_title: 面向演化动作字母表的运行时语义发现
translated_abstract: 运行时验证通常假设可观察动作具有固定的字母表。这一假设在不断演化的软件系统中变得脆弱，因为更新、重新配置或架构变更可能会重命名、拆分或合并动作，同时保持系统的高层意图不变。在这些情况下，先前有效的监视器和规约可能与运行中的系统不再对齐。本文研究了运行时语义发现问题，即在不重建全局行为模型的情况下，识别新观察到的动作是否与先前已知的动作扮演相同的操作角色。为此，我们提出了一种局部的、可在运行时计算的动作相似性概念，该概念基于执行轨迹中动作出现时的邻居上下文。我们定义了一族k-邻居等价关系，并利用它们来比较可观察字母表不同的系统。我们的方法刻意保持轻量级：它并不……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本文提出一种基于执行轨迹中邻居上下文的轻量级运行时方法，通过定义k-邻居等价关系来识别演化系统中新动作是否与已知动作具有相同的操作角色，从而在不重建全局行为模型的情况下比较可观察字母表不同的系统。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a lightweight, runtime-computable approach based on neighbor contexts in execution traces, defining a family of k-neighbor equivalences to identify whether newly observed actions play the same operational role as previously known ones, enabling comparison of systems with differing observable alphabets without reconstructing a global behavioral model.
